content:
Apple Pay is the go-to feature for iPhone users shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple just announced four new features that make Apple Pay even more useful. Here's how they work.

iOS 27 New Design

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it easier to switch between different credit cards during checkout on websites and in apps.

With the new design, you can swipe directly on the main Apple Pay checkout screen to switch between credit cards. You can also tap on a credit card to view all available Apple Pay cards in a grid layout.

The new design also makes it easier to view details for individual credit cards, including information on rewards, balances, buy now, pay later options, and more.

iOS 27 is now available in developer and public beta versions, and is expected to officially launch this fall.

Amex Rewards Points

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that allows you to use American Express Membership Rewards points to make payments.

When using an Amex card to shop online or in-app, you will see a new "Use Points" option that displays your existing Membership Rewards points balance. You can use points to pay for all or part of your purchase directly within the Apple Pay checkout flow.

Amex points redeemed through Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents per point. For example, 10,000 points can be converted to $70 to offset your purchase amount.

Tap to Provision

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a feature called Tap to Provision that works with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store purchases.

This feature is an extension of iPhone's Tap to Pay functionality, which Apple expects to launch this fall. Apple explains:

Customers can connect with a participating merchant's iPhone with just a tap, enjoying a more personalized and faster in-store shopping experience while securely sharing email and other contact information, shipping addresses, membership rewards, and more. Customers can also view items in their cart in real time, track purchased items, and ensure all discounts and offers are correctly applied.

Once complete, customers can use Apple Pay on their own iPhone to complete checkout.

Topping Up Debit Cards

Later this year, iPhone users will be able to manage debit card balances directly within the Apple Pay interface.

According to Apple, you can top up supported debit cards directly through Apple Pay in Apple Wallet or at checkout.

Summary

As Apple Pay becomes more widespread and adopted by more retailers, it's great to see Apple continuing to improve the user experience. Personally, whether shopping online or in-store, Apple Pay is basically my preferred payment method.

How often do you use Apple Pay? What's your favorite Apple Pay feature? Let us know in the comments.
